content.content:
enum AttachmentKind {
  IMAGE
  VIDEO
  FILE
}

// A product/app the boards belong to (e.g. Nxeon, Soul Pilates, studionexis).
// Boards are grouped under an App so the board page can be filtered per product.
model App {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  slug      String   @unique
  color     String?
  serverId  String?
  server    Server?  @relation(fields: [serverId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  // ---- Working context (2026-08-04) --------------------------------------
  // Where this app's code lives and how to build/deploy it, so a future Claude
  // session (or a human) can act on the RIGHT app without rediscovering the
  // layout each time. All nullable/additive (safe `db push`).
  //   codePath — absolute path to the checkout on its box (e.g. /opt/nxeon)
  //   repoUrl  — git remote, when the app has one (null for image-only apps)
  //   context  — free-form markdown: stack, build/deploy steps, conventions,
  //              gotchas. Edited by humans/Claude via the board's App settings.
  codePath  String?
  repoUrl   String?
  context   String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())
  boards    Board[]

  @@index([serverId])
}

model Board {
  id        String        @id @default(cuid())
  name      String
  appId     String?
  app       App?          @relation(fields: [appId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  createdAt DateTime      @default(now())
  columns   BoardColumn[]
  cards     Card[]

  @@index([appId])
}

model BoardColumn {
  id       String @id @default(cuid())
  boardId  String
  board    Board  @relation(fields: [boardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  name     String
  position Int    @default(0)
  cards    Card[]

  @@index([boardId])
}

model Card {
  id          String           @id @default(cuid())
  boardId     String
  board       Board            @relation(fields: [boardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  columnId    String
  column      BoardColumn      @relation(fields: [columnId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  title       String
  description String           @default("") // markdown
  type        CardType         @default(FEATURE)
  priority    CardPriority     @default(NORMAL)
  labels      String[]         @default([])
  assignee    String? // free-text ("me", "claude", a name)
  position    Int              @default(0)
  archivedAt  DateTime?
  createdAt   DateTime         @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime         @updatedAt
  attachments CardAttachment[]
  comments    CardComment[]

  @@index([boardId])
  @@index([columnId])
}

model CardAttachment {
  id         String         @id @default(cuid())
  cardId     String
  card       Card           @relation(fields: [cardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  filename   String // original name shown to the user
  storedName String // on-disk name (uuid + ext) under the board upload dir
  mime       String         @default("application/octet-stream")
  sizeBytes  Int            @default(0)
  kind       AttachmentKind @default(FILE)
  createdAt  DateTime       @default(now())

  @@index([cardId])
}

model CardComment {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  cardId     String
  card       Card     @relation(fields: [cardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorName String   @default("")
  body       String
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([cardId])
}

// ============================================================================
// WORK BOARDS (staff + admin project/task management — "the ClickUp
// alternative")
model WorkBoard {
  id          String       @id @default(cuid())
  name        String
  description String?
  archivedAt  DateTime?
  createdById String
  createdBy   User         @relation("WorkBoardCreator", fields: [createdById], references: [id])
  createdAt   DateTime     @default(now())
  columns     WorkColumn[]
  tasks       WorkTask[]
}

model WorkColumn {
  id       String     @id @default(cuid())
  boardId  String
  board    WorkBoard  @relation(fields: [boardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  name     String
  position Int        @default(0)
  tasks    WorkTask[]

  @@index([boardId])
}

model WorkTask {
  id          String               @id @default(cuid())
  boardId     String
  board       WorkBoard            @relation(fields: [boardId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  columnId    String
  column      WorkColumn           @relation(fields: [columnId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  title       String
  description String               @default("")
  priority    CardPriority         @default(NORMAL)
  assigneeId  String?
  assignee    User?                @relation("WorkTaskAssignee", fields: [assigneeId], references: [id], onDelete: SetNull)
  dueAt       DateTime?
  position    Int                  @default(0)
  archivedAt  DateTime?
  completedAt DateTime?
  createdById String
  createdBy   User                 @relation("WorkTaskCreator", fields: [createdById], references: [id])
  createdAt   DateTime             @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime             @updatedAt
  checklist   WorkChecklistItem[]
  comments    WorkTaskComment[]
  attachments WorkTaskAttachment[]

  @@index([boardId])
  @@index([columnId])
  @@index([assigneeId])
}

model WorkChecklistItem {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  taskId    String
  task      WorkTask @relation(fields: [taskId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  label     String
  done      Boolean  @default(false)
  position  Int      @default(0)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([taskId])
}

model WorkTaskComment {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  taskId    String
  task      WorkTask @relation(fields: [taskId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  authorId  String
  author    User     @relation("WorkTaskCommentAuthor", fields: [authorId], references: [id])
  body      String
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([taskId])
}

model WorkTaskAttachment {
  id           String         @id @default(cuid())
  taskId       String
  task         WorkTask       @relation(fields: [taskId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  filename     String
  storedName   String
  mime         String         @default("application/octet-stream")
  sizeBytes    Int            @default(0)
  kind         AttachmentKind @default(FILE)
  uploadedById String
  uploadedBy   User           @relation("WorkTaskAttachmentUploader", fields: [uploadedById], references: [id])
  createdAt    DateTime       @default(now())

  @@index([taskId])
}

// ---- Content: blog / guides ----

24	  const partner = await db.referralPartner.findUnique({ where: { userId: user.id } });
25	
26	  if (!partner) {
27	    // Not a partner themselves — but may still be a referred CUSTOMER of
28	    // someone else's partner link (a distinct relationship, see PartnerView's
29	    // doc comment). Surfaced on this page too, not just Billing, so it isn't
30	    // only visible somewhere a customer landing on "Partner Program" has no
31	    // reason to look.
32	    const discount = await partnerPreviewForUser(user.id);
33	    return <PartnerView partner={null} discount={discount} />;
34	  }
35	
36	  const [summary, funnel, customers, commissions, payouts] = await Promise.all([
37	    computePartnerSummary(partner.id),
38	    partnerFunnel(partner.id, partner.code),
39	    db.partnerCustomer.findMany({
40	      where: { partnerId: partner.id },
41	      orderBy: { attachedAt: "desc" },
42	      take: 500,
43	      include: { customer: { select: { name: true, email: true } } },
44	    }),
45	    db.partnerCommission.findMany({
46	      where: { partnerId: partner.id },
47	      orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" },
48	      take: 100,
49	      include: {
50	        customer: { select: { name: true, email: true } },
51	        invoice: { select: { number: true } },
52	      },
53	    }),
54	    db.partnerPayout.findMany({ where: { partnerId: partner.id }, orderBy: { createdAt: "desc" }, take: 100 }),
55	  ]);
56	  const perCustomer = await Promise.all(
57	    customers.map((c) =>
58	      db.partnerCommission.aggregate({

content.thinking:
I notice the schema's default commission rate is 20%, but the program document states 40%, matching if an admin explicitly sets that rate per partner. I'm checking whether the "locked as founding partner" clause—guaranteeing the rate never decreases even as terms change for newer partners—is actually enforced in how commissionRatePct is stored per partner.

Continuing to compare, I'm finding several mismatches: the frozen rate is only captured at accrual time, so the "never reduced" promise isn't system-enforced, just a policy claim. The "50% off first month" language doesn't match the system's "50% off first purchase" logic, and I need to verify whether referral codes actually work at checkout or only referral links do. I also see the PDF omits that dedicated-IP lines earn 0% commission and that domains are excluded from the ongoing 10% discount, both of which are real discrepancies worth flagging.

Payout methods are another sticking point — the PDF specifies Wise, PayPal, and direct deposit, but the platform-wide settings aren't configured yet, and I'm debating whether to add crypto as an option per the owner's suggestion even though that would contradict the PDF's stated terms. I think the safer choice is sticking to the three methods actually named in the PDF to avoid creating a new inconsistency.

I'll include all four payout methods including crypto since it was requested, but flag the mismatch. Then I'm cross-checking other terms against the system: the $25 minimum isn't actually configured anywhere, the monthly payout schedule contradicts the system's "paid on request" model, while the no-contract/non-exclusive/cancel-anytime terms don't conflict with anything since they're just policy statements the system doesn't need to enforce.

I'm also verifying whether checkout actually accepts a referral code, whether the "50% off first purchase" language matches what's really a first-month discount capped to one billing cycle, and confirming commissions do post in near-real-time. Given the discrepancies I've found, I'm leaning toward not publishing the PDF as-is and instead building a Terms tab that reflects what the system actually does.

I'm designing the download slot so it only appears when a PDF has been explicitly approved—checking for a file in a private directory or a setting flag rather than serving anything by default—so a mismatched document never gets exposed through the UI even if the infrastructure exists.

For the media kit, the owner's actual 72MB file failed to upload since it exceeds the 50MB non-video cap, triggering that 413/499 error. I only have the existing public assets to work with — logo, brand banners, and that zip package — so the tab should use those while I report the upload failure and its cause.

This is really outside my scope to fix as a subagent, so I should just report the upload cap issue to the caller rather than trying to resolve it myself. I've already confirmed there's nothing in staging from the owner in the last day, so no need to dig further there.

Extracting text with pdftotext should be sufficient for reviewing the PDF content. Now I want to verify the partner-discount logic around "first month" wording and check how the "creator code" field behaves at checkout.

#!/bin/bash
# Deploy a ref (default: main from /opt/nxeon) to the staging environment.
# Usage: ./scripts/deploy-staging.sh [git-ref]
set -euo pipefail
REF="${1:-main}"
cd /opt/nxeon-staging

echo "==> Syncing staging to $REF"
git fetch origin
git reset --hard "origin/$REF"

echo "==> Installing dependencies"
npm install --no-audit --no-fund 2>&1 | tail -1

echo "==> Applying database schema"
npx prisma db push --accept-data-loss 2>&1 | tail -2
npm run db:seed 2>&1 | tail -2 || true

echo "==> Building"
npm run build 2>&1 | tail -4

# next.config sets output:"standalone" but the systemd unit runs the standalone
# server.js directly (not `next start`, which Next.js explicitly does not
# support alongside output:"standalone" — it prints a warning and silently
# fails to resolve some routes, confirmed live 2026-09-10: a brand-new API
# route 404'd under `next start` on this exact build and returned 200 under
# `node .next/standalone/server.js`). The standalone output does NOT include
# public/ or .next/static/ (Next's own documented behavior) — copy them in
# fresh every build, or every static asset/route added after the last copy
# is missing until the next deploy happens to also touch this step.
echo "==> Copying static assets into the standalone server output"
rm -rf .next/standalone/public .next/standalone/.next/static
cp -r public .next/standalone/public
cp -r .next/static .next/standalone/.next/static
# geoip-lite is in next.config.ts's serverExternalPackages (kept OUT of the JS
# bundle on purpose, since it reads .dat files off its own package path at
# runtime) — but the standalone output tracer only copies files it can trace
# as JS-imported, so an externalized package's own non-JS data files are
# silently left behind. Found live 2026-09-10: this crashed EVERY request
# with an uncaught ENOENT the moment the systemd unit ran the standalone
# server.js instead of `next start` — geo-ip.ts's own try/catch around
# geoip.lookup() does NOT help, because the failure isn't confined to that
# call. Copy the package's real data/ directory in every build, same
# reasoning as public/.next/static above.
if [ -d node_modules/geoip-lite/data ]; then
  mkdir -p .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data
  cp -r node_modules/geoip-lite/data/. .next/standalone/node_modules/geoip-lite/data/
fi

# Web runs as the unprivileged 'nxeon' user. Only .next needs to be writable by
# it (Next cache); the rest stays root-owned and world-readable, and systemd
# injects .env as root. Do NOT chown the whole tree (breaks root git on .git).
echo "==> Fixing .next ownership for non-root web"
chown -R nxeon:nxeon /opt/nxeon-staging/.next 2>/dev/null || true
chmod 600 /opt/nxeon-staging/.env 2>/dev/null || true

echo "==> Restarting staging services"
systemctl restart nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
sleep 5
systemctl is-active nxeon-staging-web nxeon-staging-worker
CODE=$(curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" http://127.0.0.1:8080/)
echo "==> Staging responds: HTTP $CODE (http://$(grep ^PUBLIC_IP .env | cut -d= -f2):8080)"
[ "$CODE" = "200" ] || { echo "STAGING UNHEALTHY"; exit 1; }
echo "==> Staging deploy complete"

content.thinking:
The reset command needs my branch pushed to origin first, and since commits auto-push via the post-commit hook in this worktree, that should be fine. Now I'm designing the schema for a PartnerPayoutProfile model to store a partner's contact and manual payout details.

I'm adding an encrypted JSON field to hold method-specific payout details and notes, keeping only basic contact info as plain text, plus linking it back to ReferralPartner with an optional relation field — this is purely additive at the DB level. I should also plan a masked display summary (like partially hidden email or IBAN) so partners can verify their saved payout info without exposing it fully.

Thinking about security around who can change payout destinations, I want to avoid prefilling decrypted secrets into the form since an attacker with a hijacked session could redirect payouts to themselves; instead I'll show a masked summary and require full re-entry to change details, add a `payoutUpdatedAt` timestamp, and split the form into a prefilled contact-info section and a separate payout-method section that starts blank until the partner explicitly wants to update it.

I also want to check if there's an email helper to notify partners when their payout details change as an extra security signal, add the decrypted payout info to the admin billing-gated partner page, log an audit event on any payout profile update without exposing the actual details, and rate-limit the profile update endpoint per user.

Now onto analytics: supporting ranges like 7d/30d/90d/12m/all plus custom date bounds, bucketing by day/week/month depending on range length, and defining "all" as spanning from partner creation to now. I'm working out how to compute clicks, signups, and first-paying-conversion metrics within the range, using the customer's earliest commission timestamp to determine conversion.

I'm also defining conversion rate metrics (click→signup, signup→paid) with a caveat about cohort mismatch since these are period-based ratios not cohort-based, and figuring out how to report commission earned versus payouts received within a period versus the all-time outstanding balance.

For the time series chart, I want clicks/signups/conversions and commission plotted per bucket using the existing AreaChart component, but I'm noticing it has a fixed min-width causing horizontal scroll on mobile and hardcoded dark-mode colors that won't work well with the portal's light theme — need to check if that's acceptable or needs adjusting.

I'm also planning the top referral sources breakdown, grouping by referer host with a "Direct / no referrer" fallback for null values, and sketching out the events table columns: date, customer, product category, and commission amount.

For customers, I want to replace scattered aggregate queries with a single groupBy on customerId that pulls sum, count, and min createdAt, adding "First paid" and "Charges" columns to the table. For the Payouts tab, I'm mapping out balance summaries (lifetime earned, paid out, outstanding), a payout history table, and a recent commission ledger capped at 100 rows.

I need to keep the "how payouts work" language truthful — it's manual and arranged by contacting the team, not automated monthly payouts, so I'll preserve the existing accurate copy.

For the media kit tab, I'm sticking with the existing assets already in the brand/partner folders since the owner's large upload failed and the generated marketing zip isn't approved for publishing yet. For the terms tab, I'm expanding the existing truthful terms content a bit rather than inventing new policy language.

I'm also weighing whether to build a PDF download route for the terms page even though no approved PDF file exists yet — I think it's worth doing since it's cheap and shows the owner exactly where to drop the file, storing it at a private repo path outside the public folder rather than serving it unauthenticated.

Now I'm hitting a snag: the standalone Next.js build doesn't include arbitrary files outside traced imports, so a file dropped in a private repo folder won't actually be deployed with the server. I'm considering alternatives like an environment variable pointing to an absolute path, a database Setting storing the file location, or using outputFileTracingIncludes in next.config to force the file to be bundled.

I think the cleanest approach mirrors BOARD_UPLOAD_DIR: define something like NXEON_PARTNER_FILES_DIR with a sensible default path outside the build, so an admin can drop or upload the approved terms PDF there rather than baking it into the repo. I'm now weighing whether to expose this through a dedicated route handler versus building a full admin upload form, and leaning toward keeping it simple with just a route.

I'm sketching a route handler that requires the user to be an authenticated partner, checks whether the terms PDF exists at the configured path, and streams it back if so, returning a 404 otherwise — with the dashboard page hiding the download button when the file isn't present. I still need to decide whether this document should require authentication at all, since partner terms might reasonably be public-facing outreach material.

Since the document contains contact info like an email and WhatsApp number, it's better to keep it authenticated within the portal, while outreach can just send it as an email attachment. Media kit assets can live in the public folder since they're meant to be shared freely. For the Overview tab, I'm planning stat tiles for customers, lifetime and pending/paid earnings, funnel metrics like clicks and conversions, plus the partner link and a "what you earn" summary, possibly with a small 30-day mini-summary linking to Analytics. The Settings tab will just need a contact form and payout preference form, and now I want to verify what's available for schema validation.

Base directory for this skill: /tmp/claude-0/bundled-skills/2.1.281/89345dfcb0acd6966d8bc34efb181ad6/dataviz

# Data Visualization

A chart is **read by people and executed by you**. This skill turns "make it look
good" into a procedure with checks, so the result is right by construction rather
than by taste.

**The method here is design-system-agnostic.** Nothing in the procedure, the form
heuristic, the six checks, or the mark specs is specific to one product. A design
system supplies a small set of *parameters* (its ramps, a categorical order, a
diverging pair, a status palette, a texture, its surfaces, its filter components);
the method consumes them unchanged. A **validated default palette** is the
reference instance, fully specified in `references/palette.md`. To target your
brand, read that file's structure and substitute its values - touch nothing else.

> The single most important habit: **the color part is computable, so compute it.**
> Never eyeball whether a palette is colorblind-safe - run `scripts/validate_palette.js`.

## The procedure - do these in order

Color comes LAST. Most bad charts pick colors first.

1. **Pick the form.** What is the data's job - magnitude, identity, polarity, a
   single headline, change-over-time? The job picks the chart type, and sometimes
   the answer is *not a chart* (a stat tile or hero number). -> `references/choosing-a-form.md`
2. **Assign color by the job it does.** Categorical (identity), sequential
   (magnitude), diverging (polarity), or status (state) - each has one rule.
   Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled. -> `references/color-formula.md`
3. **VALIDATE the palette - run the script, don't reason about Delta E.**
   `node scripts/validate_palette.js "<hex,hex,...>" --mode light` (relative to
   this skill's base directory - or load it as `<script type="module">` in the
   chart's own page, where it reads
   `data-palette` off `<body>` and logs a `console.table` report). It returns
   pass/fail on the lightness band, chroma floor, adjacent-pair CVD separation,
   the normal-vision floor, and contrast. Fix anything that FAILs before continuing. Re-run for
   `--mode dark` with that mode's surface.
4. **Apply mark specs & spacers.** Thin marks, 4px rounded data-ends anchored to
   the baseline, 2px lines, >=8px markers, a 2px surface gap between fills (stacked
   segments and adjacent bars alike) and a 2px surface ring on overlapping marks,
   selective direct labels. -> `references/marks-and-anatomy.md`
5. **Add the hover layer - by default.** An HTML/SVG chart *is* interactive; ship
   a crosshair+tooltip on line/area and a per-mark hover tooltip on bar/dot/cell.
   The only form that skips it is a bare stat tile with no plot. Hit targets bigger
   than the mark; filters in one row above the charts. -> `references/interaction.md`
6. **Final accessibility pass.** For >= 2 series a legend is always present and <= 4
   are also direct-labeled (a single series needs no legend box - the title names
   it), so identity is never color-alone; a table view exists; dark mode is **selected** - its own
   steps from the same ramps, validated against the dark surface, not an automatic
   flip; texture is available for the CVD/print/forced-colors case.
7. **Render it and look at it.** The validator checks color, not layout - open or
   screenshot the output and eyeball it for label collisions, geometry, and overflow
   before calling it done.

Then check the result against **`references/anti-patterns.md`** - it is the catalog
of what goes wrong. If your chart matches an entry, it's wrong.

## Non-negotiables (true in every design system)

- **Assign categorical hues in fixed order, never cycled.** A 9th series is never a
  generated hue - it folds into "Other," small multiples, or composite encoding.
- **One axis.** Never a dual-axis chart (two y-scales). Two measures of different
  scale -> two charts, small multiples, or indexed to a common base. *(This is the
  #1 chart mistake - see anti-patterns.)*
- **Color follows the entity, never its rank.** A filter that changes the series
  count must not repaint the survivors.
- **Sequential = one hue, light->dark. Diverging = two hues + a neutral gray
  midpoint.** Never a rainbow; never a hue at the diverging midpoint.
- **Run the validator before shipping any categorical palette.** CVD Delta E >= 8 is the
  target (OKLab ×100); 6-8 is a floor that is legal ONLY with secondary encoding. A
  normal-vision floor below 15 is a hard FAIL - full-color readers can't tell the
  pair apart; re-step it on the adjacent pairlist (secondary encoding does not excuse
  this one); under `--pairs all` cut series or facet instead - see check 4. A contrast WARN
  obligates visible labels or a table view - it is not dismissable.
- **Thin marks; a legend always present for >= 2 series (none for one), with
  selective direct labels (never a number on every point); recessive grid/axes.**
- **Text wears text tokens, never the series color** - values, labels, and legends
  stay in primary/secondary/muted ink; a colored mark beside them carries identity.
- **Status colors are reserved** (good/warning/serious/critical) and never reused
  for "series 4"; they ship with an icon + label, never color alone.

## Plugging in a design system

The method is invariant; only these parameters change per system. The reference
instance - every value filled in - is `references/palette.md`.

| Parameter | What the system provides |
|---|---|
| **Ramps** | the hue scales (named steps) the palette draws from |
| **Categorical theme** | the fixed hue order (a named theme); default + alternates |
| **Sequential hue** | the default single hue for magnitude |
| **Diverging pair** | two warm/cool poles + a neutral midpoint |
| **Status palette** | good / warning / serious / critical - steps distinct from categorical |
| **Texture fill** | one directional hand-drawn fill, used at 45° / 135° |
| **Surfaces** | light & dark chart-surface colors (the validator needs these) |
| **Filter controls** | date-range & dimension controls (behavioral spec in `interaction.md`) |

To onboard a new system: fill those rows, feed its ramps to the validator, and let
it snap each slot to the nearest passing step. Structure and rules stay as written.

## Reference files

| File | What it answers |
|------|-----------------|
| `references/choosing-a-form.md` | Which chart type / is it even a chart? |
| `references/color-formula.md` | The four jobs, the six checks, snap-to-passing |
| `references/marks-and-anatomy.md` | Mark specs, spacers, labels, figures, hero number |
| `references/interaction.md` | Tooltips & hover, filters & time ranges |
| `references/components.md` | The pieces a chart is made of - build each in plain HTML |
| `references/anti-patterns.md` | **What goes wrong - check every chart against this** |
| `references/palette.md` | **The reference palette instance** - every parameter, filled in; swap for your brand's |
| `scripts/validate_palette.js` | Runnable six-checks validator (run it; don't eyeball) |

I'll also add a collapsible "view as table" details element under the chart for accessibility, listing the bucket values directly.

Now I'm laying out the implementation files: a Prisma schema addition for a PartnerPayoutProfile model with its relation, a server-only analytics module for parsing date ranges and computing metrics, and a shared payout profile module defining methods and validation schemas.

I'm splitting server actions into their own file, adding an authenticated PDF endpoint for partner terms, and planning the dashboard page structure. For components, I'll rework PartnerView.tsx to keep the landing and dashboard shell while introducing separate PartnerAnalytics.tsx and PartnerSettings.tsx components, plus extending charts.tsx with a new BarChart.

For date range handling, I'm designing a parseRange utility that normalizes preset and custom ranges into UTC start/end dates with appropriate bucketing (day/week/month), validating custom ranges for sane bounds and falling back to a 30-day default with an error flag if invalid.

For "all", I need the true earliest activity date, so I'm taking the minimum of the partner's creation date and the earliest click or attachment tied to their code, since clicks could predate partner signup. Bucket granularity switches from day to week to month as the span grows, with weeks starting Monday UTC, and I'm scoping the click/attachment queries to the resolved date range.

For signups I'm pulling partnerCustomer records by attachedAt in range; for conversions, grouping by customer and taking the earliest non-void commission timestamp to represent first conversion. For commissions I'm fetching a capped set with customer and invoice details for the table, but computing sums via a separate grouped aggregate to avoid truncation, and pulling all raw commission rows unbounded for the chart so bucketed totals stay accurate.

Now I'm thinking through how to frame the paying conversion rate — rather than a simple period-over-period ratio, I want a cohort view: of the customers who signed up in this window, how many have ever paid, alongside a separate count of first-time paid conversions that happened to land in this period.

For click→signup, I'm avoiding the existing page's uncapped math and instead using click-level attribution (converted clicks ÷ total clicks in period) since that stays bounded and honestly reflects what led to a signup.

Now I'm setting up a shared pure module for partner payout settings, starting with the payout method definitions (PayPal, Wise, bank transfer).

Then I'm mapping out the detail fields required per method: PayPal needs an email, Wise needs an email and account holder name, bank transfer needs an account name plus either IBAN/SWIFT or account/routing numbers, and crypto needs a network selection (Bitcoin, ERC-20, TRC-20, Solana, Polygon, or other) along with the asset type.

I'm planning a discriminated union schema in Zod v4 keyed on the payout method, along with masking logic for display purposes—showing partial emails, last-4 digits of account numbers, and truncated wallet addresses. For storage, I'm thinking the payout method stays as plain text while the sensitive details get JSON-encrypted, with a masked summary computed server-side for safe display.

For contact info, I'm weighing whether to reuse ReferralPartner's existing contactEmail field or keep the partner-provided contact separate to avoid overwriting admin-set data—I'll go with keeping them distinct and label it as partner-provided on the admin view. Now I'm sketching the action signature for saving partner contact info, starting with user authorization checks.

I decide to only block payout editing during impersonation, not contact info changes, since contact edits are low-risk for admins to assist with. I'm defining the payout save action, enforcing ownership by looking up the partner record via the authenticated user's ID rather than trusting any client-supplied partner ID, and adding rate limiting plus an audit log entry for payout changes.

When payout details change, I send a best-effort security notification email to the user. On the admin side, I'm rendering the partner's decrypted payout preferences as a read-only card using the existing shell's styling, gating access behind the billing area permission since that's the team responsible for payouts.

For the terms route, I'm authenticating the current user and letting either the partner themselves or an admin through, returning 404 otherwise. I locate the partner terms PDF on disk, check it exists, then stream it back with proper PDF headers—content-disposition set to force download with a fixed filename, cache-control set to prevent caching, and nosniff for security. The file path comes from an environment variable with a sensible default.

I'm setting up a client-side tabs array for the partner dashboard with overview and analytics entries, each carrying a key, label, and icon.

I'm thinking through how running `npx prisma generate` resolves the CLI binary and the @prisma/client package location—there's a risk it resolves from its own real install path instead of the project directory, which could cause it to write generated output to the wrong place.

Since editing the schema generator to force an explicit output path isn't an option without reverting later, I decide the safest approach is to just test it now: since the shared client already contains my schema changes, running generate again with the unchanged schema would write identical content even if it lands in the wrong location, so I can safely observe where it actually writes without causing new harm.

With that safe, I'm designing additive schema changes for creator invites on PartnerInvite: a `kind` field distinguishing LOGIN vs CREATOR invites, optional `name`/`note` fields, resend tracking (`lastSentAt`, `sendCount`), and an `overrideEmailMatch` flag for admin overrides. I'm weighing how to track email open status without a new field, favoring a lookup by email/template/timestamp against EmailLog instead. The tricky part is that `partnerId` is currently required, but CREATOR invites have no partner until claimed, and making that column nullable is a real schema alteration I need to think through carefully.

Making `partnerId` nullable turns out to be a safe, non-destructive relaxation of the NOT NULL constraint, so I'll go that route rather than creating placeholder partners -- existing code referencing `invite.partner` will just need null handling, which TypeScript will surface. I'm sticking with extending PartnerInvite rather than adding a separate CreatorInvite model, and adding a `ratePct` field defaulting to 40 so admins can adjust the commission rate per invite if needed. Now I'm sketching the claim flow starting with the email link containing a token.

For the claim page itself, I'm thinking it should use the AuthShell styling since creators land there before being fully in the dashboard. Logged-out users would see the invite summary with options to register or sign in, both carrying the token through a `next=` redirect param -- I need to verify that pattern is supported on both login and register pages. For logged-in users, I need to validate the invite state and check email matching, with a fallback message if the signed-in email doesn't match the invited one, plus an admin-controlled `allowAnyEmail` override for flexibility.

For the code picker, I'm setting up an 8-character uppercase input with debounced live availability checks against a rate-limited server action, then submitting the claim through another server action. The actual claim logic runs as a transaction: it re-validates the invite atomically, creates the ReferralPartner record populated from the invite's details, links the invite back to the new partner, and handles the edge case where the chosen code gets taken in a race, before redirecting into the partner dashboard.

I'm also defining validation rules for partner codes -- normalizing to uppercase, enforcing a 3-8 character alphanumeric pattern, and building out a reserved-word blocklist to prevent codes like ADMIN, STAFF, or brand names from being claimed.

For impersonation protection, I'll check both raw and leetspeak-normalized versions of codes (translating substitutions like 0→O, 1→I, 3→E) against sensitive terms like NXEON, ADMIN, STAFF, SUPPORT, and OFFICIAL, plus run a basic profanity filter.

I'll use exact matches for ambiguous words like RAPE, FAG, DICK, SEX, ASS, KKK, NAZI, HITLER, PORN, but substring matching for clearly unambiguous ones like FUCK, SHIT, CUNT, NIGG, FAGGOT, BITCH, WHORE. Now I need to handle the collision issue with existing ReferralPartner codes being uppercase.

I also realize I need to check collisions against User.referralCode too, since a creator picking a code matching an existing user's peer referral code would hijack that user's referral links -- partner codes take precedence in the registration flow, so this must be blocked with case-insensitive matching. I should check the referralCode generation format for length and confirm there's no placeholder collision case to worry about, then move on to rate limiting the sponsor code check endpoint.

Now I'm mapping out the admin "Invite a creator" flow: an emails textarea (up to 25, comma or newline separated), optional name for single invites, channel/note, default rate and expiry, and an override checkbox for claiming with a different email. On submit, each email gets checked for existing pending invites or existing partner accounts before creating a new invite and sending mail, returning per-email results with the one-time link and send status, followed by a "Creator invites" table showing email, note, and send timestamps.

Status column should cover Accepted (with partner link/code), Revoked, Expired, Opened, Sent, or Email failed, with Resend (rotate token/expiry, resend, show link) and Revoke (pending only) actions gated behind the same requireArea("billing") check used elsewhere. content.thinking:
The media kit repeats the same discrepancies — first month, $25 minimum, monthly payouts, "use my code" language — and adds product claims like "70,000+ mods" and "one-click mod install" that conflict with my earlier note that no mod installer actually exists, since they sell file/SFTP access instead. There's also mention of a mod menu feature and a creator ad video that seem to contradict that.

I'm noting these mod figures are likely ecosystem-wide stats from CurseForge or Modrinth rather than site-specific numbers, and per the codebase rule against fabricating stats, I should verify whether a one-click installer actually exists by checking for modrinth or curseforge references in the code. I also see inaccuracies around "dedicated IPv4" for VPS plans (which are actually NAT-based with SSH via DNAT), and the shared hosting claims need verification since that provisioner may still be gated behind a feature flag. Given these mismatches match the same issues found in the PDF terms, my decision is not to publish the media kit as-is.

The PNG brand assets (logos, icon, banner) look safe to publish separately though, so I'll check those images along with the creator assets page showing overlay templates to see if they correspond to the same brand files.

content.content:
## Creator Partner Program — agency/KOL commission + a real customer discount

**What it does.** An agency or content creator gets a permanent link. Every customer who signs up
through it is attached to that partner FOR LIFE (one partner per customer, enforced by a DB unique
constraint) and gets a real, sitewide discount for as long as they stay a customer — **50% off their
first purchase of any service except a domain, then 10% off every purchase after that, forever**
(new orders AND renewals). The partner earns a **lifetime commission** (their own negotiated
`commissionRatePct`, default 20%) on every qualifying charge that customer ever makes, with one
carve-out: a dedicated-IP add-on line earns the partner 0% (everything else on the same
order/renewal still earns the full rate).

This is a DIFFERENT program from "Refer & earn" (`User.referralCode`, the row above this one) — a
peer-to-peer, one-time wallet bonus. A single `?ref=`/`nxeon_ref` cookie can only ever mean ONE of
the two: at registration (`lib/actions.ts` `register()`), an ACTIVE `ReferralPartner.code` match
always wins over a `User.referralCode` match, so nobody double-dips a partner commission AND a peer
referral bonus off the same signup.

**Data model** (`prisma/schema.prisma`):

| Model | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `ReferralPartner` | The partner: `code` (unique, uppercase), `commissionRatePct` (per-partner, frozen onto each commission row at accrual), `status` (ACTIVE/PAUSED — pausing stops BOTH new commission AND the customer discount), optional `userId` login |
| `PartnerCustomer` | The lifetime attachment. `customerId` UNIQUE — one partner per customer, ever. `firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` (null until their first discounted purchase; null = 50% tier, set = 10% tier forever) |
| `PartnerCommission` | One row per qualifying PAID invoice, `invoiceId` UNIQUE (idempotent). `baseCents` = net charge minus that invoice's `dedicatedIpCents` — the dedicated-IP exclusion |
| `PartnerPayout` | A REAL payment made to the partner off-wallet (bank/Wise/PayPal), can be partial. Balance = `sum(PartnerCommission, status != VOID) − sum(PartnerPayout)` — NOT derived from commission-row status alone (see the model's own doc comment for why a partial payout needs a separate ledger) |
| `PartnerInvite` | A pending invite for a brand-new (non-customer) partner login — token-hash/expiry, mirrors `OrgInvite`'s mechanics |
| `ReferralClick` (existing, previously unused) | One row per real link click — `code`, `ipHash`, `referer`, `convertedUserId` (best-effort, set at registration to the most recent unconverted click for that code) |
| `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents` | How much of that invoice's net amount is the dedicated-IP surcharge — a real typed column, populated by every charge path that can bill one (`lib/order.ts`, `lib/game-order.ts`, `worker/billing.ts`), never inferred by parsing line items after the fact |

**The links.** `nxeon.cloud/partner/<code>` (`app/partner/[code]/route.ts`) is the REAL link partners
are given — it records a `ReferralClick` row, then sets the `nxeon_ref` cookie and 302s to
`/register`, exactly like the older `/r/<code>` (peer-referral short link), which now ALSO records a
click (same table — its own schema comment always said it covers both code namespaces).

**Automatic attachment.** `register()` (`lib/actions.ts`) reads `nxeon_ref`; if it matches an ACTIVE
partner code, `attachCustomerToPartnerByCode` (`lib/partner-commission.ts`) creates the
`PartnerCustomer` row right there — no admin action needed for the normal case. `adminAttachCustomer`
(`lib/actions-partner.ts`) remains for support/edge cases (attaching an existing account by email).

**The customer discount** — pure math in `lib/partner-discount.ts` (`PARTNER_FIRST_PURCHASE_PCT` =
50, `PARTNER_RECURRING_PCT` = 10), DB resolution in `lib/partner-pricing.ts`
(`partnerDiscountForNewOrder`, `partnerDiscountForRenewal`, `partnerPreviewForCode`/`ForUser` for
pre-purchase marketing messaging). Wired into:
- `lib/order.ts` `orderQuote`/`placeOrder` (VPS) and `lib/game-order.ts` `gameOrderQuote`/
  `placeGameOrder` (game servers) — the discount is folded into `chargeCents` itself (displayed ===
  charged), gets its OWN line on the invoice, and the first-purchase slot is claimed ATOMICALLY
  inside the same transaction that debits the wallet (`claimPartnerFirstPurchase`) — a lost race (the
  same customer's own concurrent "first" order) keeps the already-quoted price rather than
  recomputing mid-transaction (an accepted, narrow, low-severity edge case: a customer can only ever
  race against their OWN other order).
- `lib/renewal-charge.ts` `renewalCharge` — `RenewalPrices.partnerDiscountPercent` (optional, 0 by
  default), always resolved via `partnerDiscountForRenewal` (a renewal is never anyone's first
  purchase), stacks with the pre-existing one-time retention offer (retention first, partner discount
  on what's left). Wired into every real renewal path in `worker/billing.ts` (the automatic sweep,
  the saved-card auto-charge, the renewal-reminder email amount, the suspended-account
  auto-recovery) and `lib/actions.ts` `renewNow`.
- **Visible before the first purchase**, per the product requirement: the public `/pricing` page
  reads the `nxeon_ref` cookie (anonymous) or the real attachment (signed in) and shows a real banner;
  the deploy wizard (`components/nx/DeployView.tsx`) shows a live "Partner discount — 50%/10% off"
  badge next to the coupon/promo badges, sourced from the same `orderQuote`/`gameOrderQuote` result
  the wizard already prices from (`lib/nx/quote.ts`, `lib/nx/quote-game.ts`) — not a second formula.
- **Hosting, business email and domains do NOT carry this discount yet** (domains are excluded by
  spec; hosting/email have no coupon-style discount plumbing to extend today) — a real, flagged
  follow-up, not silently missing (the wizard's price object honestly reports 0%/NONE for them).

**Commission dedicated-IP exclusion** — `commissionableBaseCents(netCents, dedicatedIpCents)`
(`lib/partner-commission.ts`, pure, unit-tested) = `max(0, netCents − dedicatedIpCents)`. Every
accrual path (`accrueCommissionForInvoice`, called by the inline post-order/post-renewal hooks AND
the background `reconcilePartnerCommissions` sweep) reads `Invoice.dedicatedIpCents` and excludes it
— never a string match against a line-item description.

**Admin** (`/admin/partners`, `/admin/partners/[id]`, `lib/actions-partner.ts`,
`components/admin/PartnerControls.tsx`): create/manage partners and rates (existing), attach/detach
customers (existing), plus new: real click→signup→conversion funnel (`partnerFunnel`), the real
`/partner/<code>` link, **invite a brand-new login** (`adminCreatePartnerInvite` — a public accept
page at `/partner/invite/accept?token=...` creates the account, since the invitee has none yet;
mirrors `OrgInvite`'s token/hash/expiry, not its `requireUser()`-gated redemption), and **record a
partial/specific payout** (`adminRecordPartnerPayout`) alongside the existing full-settle
(`adminSettlePartnerCommission`, now payout-ledger-aware).

**Partner portal** (`/dashboard/partner`, `components/nx/PartnerView.tsx`): unchanged sections
(customers, commission ledger) plus new: real click/signup/conversion stats, the real `/partner/
<code>` link, a payout-history table, a media kit (downloads the app's own real `/logo.png`, `/
nx-mark.png`, `/brand/bimi-logo.svg`, plus two new on-brand promo SVG banners at `/brand/partner/`),
and a terms panel stating the partner's REAL `commissionRatePct` (never a hardcoded blanket rate —
partners are on genuinely different negotiated rates) and that payout method/minimum is not yet
configured platform-wide (nothing invented).

**Tests.** `test/partner-discount.test.ts` — pure arithmetic, no DB: discount tier resolution (not
attached / paused partner / domain → NONE; first purchase → 50%; used → 10%), the dedicated-IP
commission-exclusion boundary cases (IP-only order, mixed-addon order, no-IP order, corrupt/negative
input), and `renewalCharge` integration (partner discount stacking with the retention offer, applied
before tax, clamped, broken out via the new `ipCents`/`partnerDiscountCents` fields).

**Verified against a real, isolated database** (not the shared dev/staging/prod ones — a fresh
`nxeon_partner_dev` Postgres database + its own worktree, per this codebase's isolation discipline):
a real Chromium (Playwright) run through `/partner/<code>` → registration → the live `/pricing`
banner → the deploy wizard's discount badge, confirmed against the database (`ReferralClick.
convertedUserId` set, `PartnerCustomer` created); then two real orders placed through the actual
`orderQuote`/`placeOrder` code path (not a mock) — the first billed exactly 50% off with
`firstPurchaseDiscountUsedAt` correctly stamped, the second (with a real nonzero dedicated-IP charge)
billed exactly 10% off with the invoice correctly itemising the base plan, the IP line and the
discount line summing to the charged total, and the resulting `PartnerCommission.baseCents`
correctly excluding just the IP portion; then the real admin dashboard (`/admin/partners/[id]`)
independently confirmed: 4 real link clicks, 1 signed up, 1 converted, and lifetime commission
matching the two orders' commission exactly ($4.47).

/**
 * Refuse to write to a database nobody deliberately pointed us at.
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE INCIDENT THIS EXISTS FOR (2026-07-26)
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * An agent ran `prisma/seed.ts` from a scratch working tree. That tree had its
 * `node_modules` SYMLINKED to /opt/nxeon/node_modules, so `@prisma/client`
 * resolved through the symlink, and Prisma's dotenv loader walked up from the
 * REAL module location and loaded `/opt/nxeon/.env` — the PRODUCTION env. The
 * seed therefore connected to the production database `nxeon` while every human
 * signal (the cwd, the checkout, the intent) said "scratch".
 *
 * It happened to be a pure `upsert` seed, so it did no damage. That is luck, not
 * a control. The same accident with `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`, or with
 * a seed that had grown a `deleteMany`, destroys a live hosting platform's
 * customer records.
 *
 * The root cause is NOT "the seed was careless". It is that a writing script
 * inherits its target from ambient environment resolution — a mechanism with no
 * confirmation step, which resolves silently and can be wrong for reasons that
 * are invisible at the call site (a symlink three directories away).
 *
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * THE CONTROL
 * ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
 * A writing script must state, out loud, which database it believes it is about
 * to write to. The operator states it independently, via `NXEON_DB_TARGET`. The
 * script runs only if the two agree.
 *
 *     NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_staging npx tsx prisma/seed.ts
 *
 * This is deliberately NOT a "--force"/"--yes" flag. A blanket confirmation
 * answers "do you want to proceed?", and in the incident above the honest answer
 * was yes — the operator did want to seed, just not THAT database. Naming the
 * target answers the question that was actually wrong. An operator who types
 * `NXEON_DB_TARGET=nxeon_scratch` while the environment silently resolves to
 * `nxeon` gets a refusal and a diff, which is exactly the moment the symlink
 * becomes visible.
 *

input.message:
## What I built, and one thing to fix first

Everything is on branch **feat/partner-dashboard-tabs**, in 4 commits based on main 7d7bd0e0 and pushed to origin: d60a7206, 2d6e7a18, 6a1166ca, 7586a7ec. `npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean. Only explicit paths were committed. Nothing was promoted and no real creator was emailed.

**Fix first:** my first `npx prisma generate` in the worktree went through the node_modules symlink. At 17:47:48 it rewrote **/opt/nxeon/node_modules/.prisma/client** using my schema, which adds the new model and the new invite columns. I tried to regenerate it from /opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma, but the permission classifier denied it.
- The prod web is not affected. Its standalone copy was built at 17:47:28, before this happened.
- `nxeon-worker` (tsx from /opt/nxeon) will load this client on its next restart. The change is additive, so existing queries still work, but it is not prod's client.
- **Please run `cd /opt/nxeon && npx prisma generate`.**
- After that I switched the worktree to its own gitignored `node_modules` directory with a private `@prisma/client`, and generated with an explicit local output path.

## 1. The owner's uploads
- The "Creator Kit" card (id `cmuk3p1bn013xhllnqbrcjg19`) had no files at first. Two uploads of a 72 MB file failed at 17:40 and 17:41 (nginx 499). The board caps non-video attachments at 50 MB, and the failure never reached the owner as an error. This is worth a separate fix.
- At 17:45 the owner re-uploaded **7 files**:
  - the terms PDF, byte-identical to the earlier one on the "Full reachout" card
  - `Nxeon_Creator_Media_Kit_v3.pdf` (12 slides)
  - `logo.png`, `logo transparent.png`, `Untitled design.png`, `icon.png`
  - `nxlabs logo.png`
- The four Nxeon logo PNGs are now in `public/brand/partner/` as `nxeon-wordmark`, `-logo-transparent`, `-logo-dark` and `-mark`. **I left out `nxlabs logo.png`** because it's a different brand; the owner decides.
- **Neither PDF is published.** Both contradict the live program:
  - "50% off the first month". The system gives 50% off the first purchase of any term, and domains are excluded.
  - "$25 USD minimum payout" and "monthly payouts". Nothing configures or enforces either; payouts are arranged by hand on request.
  - "Use my code" and "tied to your referral code". There is no code field at checkout or register. Attribution only happens through the link or cookie at signup, and existing accounts aren't attached.
  - "All services purchased and renewed". Dedicated-IP lines earn 0%, and wallet top-ups and refunds are excluded.
  - "Founding rate never reduced". Admins can still change the rate.
- The media kit also needs these product claims checked: "70,000+ mods / 14B+ downloads", "one-click modpack install", "dedicated IPv4" on VPS plans, and the web-hosting features.
- The PDFs are served only to partners (and admins) through `app/api/creator-partner/[doc]/route.ts`, from `/opt/nxeon/partner-files/`. To publish once corrected, copy them to `creator-partner-terms.pdf` and `creator-media-kit.pdf` (`install -o nxeon -m 0644 …`). A download button appears only when the file exists.
- The Settings tab also offers **crypto** payouts, which your brief asked for but neither PDF lists.

## 2. Partner page tabs (`?tab=`, keyboard-accessible, Back button works)
- **Overview:** the stat tiles, the click/signup/conversion funnel, the link with share buttons and code, "What you earn", and a nudge to add a payout method.
- **Analytics:** a server-side date range (7d / 30d / 90d / 12m / all / custom from–to).
  - Totals: clicks, signups, paying conversions, rates, commission earned, and pending vs paid.
  - Four bar charts (clicks, signups and conversions per day, week or month, plus commission) in a new dependency-free `components/ui/bar-chart.tsx`, with hover/keyboard tooltips and a table view.
  - Top sources come from `ReferralClick.referer`. **There is no UTM capture**, and many apps send no referrer, which shows as "Direct / not shared".
  - A dated table of commission events. Its product column never shows the customer's server or domain names.
- **Customers:** signup date, first paid purchase, charge count and commission earned.
- **Payouts:** earned, paid and owed; payout history; the masked preferred method; the commission ledger.
- **Media kit:** the brand assets above.
- **Terms:** the program exactly as the platform applies it.
- **Settings:** contact name, email, phone, Discord and social, plus the preferred manual payout method (PayPal, Wise, bank with IBAN/SWIFT or account/routing, crypto) and a note.
  - Payout details and the note are encrypted with `lib/crypto-box.ts`, validated with zod, rate-limited, and audit-logged without the details.
  - Changing the method is refused while impersonating and emails the account a security notice.
  - The partner only ever sees a masked summary. Billing-area admins see the full details on `/admin/partners/<id>`, under "Where to send it".

## 3. Creator invites (all of your follow-up requirements)
- **Drafts:** creating an invite never sends it. A draft's token hash is random, so it can't be claimed.
- **Sending:** "Send", "Resend" and "Send all drafts" each confirm first, listing the count and every recipient. "Send all drafts" re-checks the count on the server. Every send rotates the token and sets a 14-day expiry, and the admin sees the new link once.
- **Status per invite:** draft, sent, opened, not delivered, accepted (with the chosen code), expired or revoked.
- **Preview:** shows the exact subject and HTML the send path renders, with the creator's real name and a placeholder token.
- **CSV prefill:** from the stored master CSV (found by attachment name) or an uploaded CSV. Matching is by exact email only, and unmatched emails are listed.
- **Claim:** register or log in with `next=`, then choose a code.
  - Codes are 3–8 letters/digits, case-insensitive, and stored uppercase.
  - Codes are checked for reserved words, impersonation and profanity (including 0→O style swaps), and for collisions with partner codes, coupons and customers' referral codes.
  - Availability is checked live and again at claim. Both checks are rate-limited.
  - The account's email must match the invite unless the admin ticks the override.
  - The claimed partner's Settings start with the invite's name and channel link.
- **Batch script:** `scripts/partner-invite-batch.ts --emails --csv [--dry-run] [--preview <email> --out]`. It only creates drafts, is idempotent, and prints a table.
- The runbook is in DOCUMENTATION.md ("Inviting a batch of creators — the runbook"), along with the Creator Partner Program section and a dated change-history entry.
- I did not load or touch `/root/nxeon-creator-invites/batch-2026-09-27.json` or the master list's real emails.
- The older LOGIN invite (`adminCreatePartnerInvite`) is unchanged and still emails as soon as it's created.

## Schema (all additive or relaxing)
- New model **`PartnerPayoutProfile`** with plain contact fields and encrypted payout details.
- **`PartnerInvite`** gains `kind`, `name`, `note`, `ratePct`, `allowAnyEmail`, `channelUrl`, `primaryGame`, `country`, `subscribers`, `lastSentAt` (null means draft) and `sendCount`.
- `partnerId` becomes nullable.

## Verification
- **Staging deploy:** `deploy-staging.sh` succeeded at 2d6e7a18 (built and healthy, schema applied at 18:49). It could not be clicked through: **the staging admin password in `/root/nxeon-staging-credentials.txt` is rejected**, and without an admin I can't create an invite or partner through the UI. I made no DB writes to get around it.
- **Full end-to-end run:** I did it on an isolated database instead, `nxeon_partner_tabs_dev`, seeded normally, running `next dev` from the worktree, with real UI flows only and example.com addresses. **All 58 Playwright checks passed.** Nothing was delivered; every email log row says "SMTP not configured".
- **Batch script:** tested dry-run, create, and a re-run that skipped everything, plus `--preview`.
- **Staging collision:** another session was deploying `release/nxm-launch` at the same time. It collided with my first deploy, which failed with ENOENT, and their build then hung for about 25 minutes.
- **Staging now runs their a9153fbd, not my branch.** Their redeploy at 19:08 ran `db push --accept-data-loss`, which dropped my new table and columns from `nxeon_staging` (test data only). My last three small UI fixes (the preview modal sitting under the cookie notice, the payout form not folding after save, and media tiles overflowing) are verified on the dev DB but not on staging. I didn't redeploy over their active work.
- **Rollout warning:** any environment deployed from a ref without this schema, after this branch, will drop these fields the same way.

## Screenshots
In `/tmp/claude-0/-root/ec6fa978-d80b-4147-9982-eea470598e2c/scratchpad/partner/`, all `dev-*.png`:
- every tab at 1440 and 390 (`dev-tab-*`)
- analytics 7-day hover and custom range
- settings: welcome and saved
- claim flow: signed out, code rejected, code available (1440 and 390)
- admin: drafts from CSV, drafts table, email preview, invite sent, accepted invite, partner detail with payout details

Results are in `dev-verify-results.json`. The rendered email previews are `dev-script-preview.html` and `invite-preview-test.html`.

## Other notes
- A 40% rate shows a "Custom tier" chip. That mapping comes from the existing tiers in `lib/nx/rewards`.
- Customer emails are not masked on the Customers tab or the events table. The page never masked them; the owner may want to decide.
- **Leftovers to remove when you're done:** the `nxeon_partner_tabs_dev` database (`sudo -u postgres dropdb nxeon_partner_tabs_dev`), and the worktree's `.env` and local `node_modules` (both gitignored).

content.text: I've sent my full report to your caller.
